name: sol_basics_vi_ovi_12
description: Unexpected revert in OpenZeppelin SignatureChecker.isValidSignatureNow instead of returning false
question: The source file in `source` calls OpenZeppelin's SignatureChecker.isValidSignatureNow (from a version >=4.1.0 and <4.7.1) to validate a signature that may come from a contract signer, and treats a false return as the only invalid-signature outcome without wrapping the call in try/catch or otherwise handling the case where the target does not properly implement EIP-1271, so an unexpected revert can occur where non-reverting invalid-signature handling was assumed. This excludes code that only validates signatures from EOAs via ecrecover without using SignatureChecker, code that wraps the isValidSignatureNow call in try/catch to handle reverts gracefully, and code confirmed to use OpenZeppelin version >=4.7.1.
criteria: calls SignatureChecker.isValidSignatureNow(signer, hash, signature) directly and branches on the boolean result without any try/catch, assuming it can never revert
passes an arbitrary or user-supplied contract address as the signer into isValidSignatureNow and treats a revert-free false return as the sole rejection path for invalid signatures

uses SignatureChecker.isValidSignatureNow inside a function that must not revert (e.g., a batch process or fallback validation path) and does not guard the call against unexpected reverts from malformed EIP-1271 return data
